newsitem.title: USA: Skater Scott Hamilton undergoes cancer surgery.
newsitem.headline: Skater Scott Hamilton undergoes cancer surgery.

text.p: Olympic gold medalist and four-time World figure skating champion Scott Hamilton successfully underwent surgery on Tuesday for testicular cancer.
"Scott had uncomplicated surgery and there were no signs of active cancer," said surgeon Eric Klein, who performed the four-hour operation in Cleveland.
"His chances for cure and complete recovery are excellent," said Klein, head of the Urologic Oncology section at the Cleveland Clinic Foundation.

The 38-year-old figure skating star, who was diagnosed with testicular cancer in March while headlining a 60-city U.S. ice show tour, had been suffering from severe stomach pains for several weeks prior to surgery.

Test results confirmed that a tumour originally found in Hamilton's lower abdomen caused by cancer cells within the testicle region, had been arrested as a result of chemotherapy during the past two and a half months, Hamilton's Los Angeles-based publicist said.
Hamilton is expected to resume skating by September.
